en.title: Oil tanker carrying 27 Indians attacked with limpet mines in Strait of Hormuz
en.dek: A Panama‑flagged tanker was hit by limpet mines, causing a fire but no injuries to its Indian crew.
facts: 27 Indian seafarers aboard the Panama‑flagged tanker were targeted with limpet mines.
A small boat attached two mines to the vessel's hull, causing a fire in the engine room.
Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all crew were safe and sustained no injuries.
The incident occurred about 25 nautical miles northeast of Oman's Khasab.
UK Maritime Trade Operations reported the fire was extinguished and there was no environmental impact.
body: A Panama‑flagged tanker was hit by limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz, about 25 nautical miles northeast of Oman's Khasab, according to German broadcaster Deutsche Welle. The attack caused a fire in the engine room, but the crew remained unharmed. The incident was reported by maritime security sources on Friday.
Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all 27 Indian seafarers aboard were safe and sustained no injuries. He also noted that two Indians on another tanker attacked on October 29 were safe.

UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that the fire was extinguished, the crew was safe, and there was no environmental impact. The incident marks the first known successful use of limpet mines against a vessel in the waterway since the US‑Iran war began in February.

The Strait of Hormuz is a vital chokepoint for oil and gas transport, and attacks on ships have risen to the highest level since the war began, according to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy. Other vessels, such as the RITI, have also been targeted, with Oman rescuing 25 crew members from a burning ship, as reported by The Straits Times. US Central Command said its forces conduct nightly missions to protect commercial shipping.
en.context: The Strait of Hormuz is a vital chokepoint for oil transport, carrying about a fifth of global crude. Since the US‑Iran war began in February, attacks on vessels have increased, and US forces have conducted nightly missions to protect commercial shipping.
